He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte 49ers]] and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]]. ==High school career== Young played basketball for [[St. Mary's Ryken High School]] in [[Leonardtown, Maryland]] in his first two years. For his junior season, he transferred to [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]] due to a coaching change at St. Mary's Ryken. At DeMatha Catholic, he played alongside teammates: [[Hunter Dickinson]], [[Justin Moore (basketball)|Justin Moore]], [[Earl Timberlake]], and [[Tyrell Ward]]. As a junior, Young averaged 11.7 points per game and helped his team win the [[Washington Catholic Athletic Conference]] title.{{cite news|first=Samantha|last=Pell|title=Stock rises for three-star guard Jahmir Young after standout showing at Peach Jam|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2018/07/17/stock-rises-for-three-star-guard-jahmir-young-after-standout-showing-at-peach-jam/|newspaper=[[The Washington 6, 2018|url-status=live}} On the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, he played for Team Takeover and won a [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League#Peach Jam|Peach Jam]] title.{{cite web|title=Charlotte 49ers freshman Jahmir Young making big impact|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/mens-basketball/article237477239.html|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=November 18, 2021|url-status=live}} As a senior, Young earned All-Conference honors and was ranked a top 10 senior in Maryland.{{cite web|first=Bryson|last=Foster|title=Young looks to follow up breakout freshman campaign|url=https://www.ninertimes.com/sports/mens_basketball/young-looks-to-follow-up-breakout-freshman-campaign/article_2800fd6e-2441-11eb-9391-83ae47bb513e.html|work=Niner Times|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=November 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327013117/https://www.ninertimes.com/sports/mens_basketball/young-looks-to-follow-up-breakout-freshman-campaign/article_2800fd6e-2441-11eb-9391-83ae47bb513e.html|archive-date=March 27, 2021|url-status=live}} A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]] over offers from [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]], [[Old Dominion Monarchs basketball|Old Dominion]] and [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=McFadden|title=Three-star guard Jahmir Young commits to Charlotte|url=https://insidethelockerroom.net/2018/10/27/three-star-guard-jahmir-young-commits-to-charlotte/|work=Inside the Locker Room|date=October 27, 2018|access-date=November 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303202325/https://insidethelockerroom.net/2018/10/27/three-star-guard-jahmir-young-commits-to-charlotte/|archive-date=March 3, 2021|url-status=live}} ==College career== As a freshman at Charlotte, Young averaged 12.5 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game, and was named Third Team All-[[Conference USA]] (C-USA) and Freshman of the Year. He was an eight-time C-USA Freshman of the Week honoree, becoming the fourth player in league history to do so.{{cite web|title=Young Earns Eighth C-USA Freshman of the Week Award|url=https://charlotte49ers.com/story.aspx?filename=young-earns-eighth-c-usa-freshman-of-the-week-award&file_date=2/24/2020|website=Charlotte49ers.com|date=February 24, 2020|access-date=November 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211103144449/https://charlotte49ers.com/story.aspx?filename=young-earns-eighth-c-usa-freshman-of-the-week-award&file_date=2%2F24%2F2020|archive-date=November 3, 2021|url-status=live}} On December 19, 2020, Young scored a sophomore season-high 27 points in a 76–72 win against [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]].{{cite web|title=Young scores 27 to lift Charlotte past NC A&T 76-72|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401262858|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=November 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211103144443/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401262858|archive-date=November 3, 2021|url-status=live}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, earning First Team All-C-USA honors.{{cite web|title=Young Named First Team All-Conference USA|url=https://charlotte49ers.com/news/2021/3/8/mens-basketball-young-named-first-team-all-conference-usa.aspx|website=Charlotte49ers.com|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=November 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309052218/https://charlotte49ers.com/news/2021/3/8/mens-basketball-young-named-first-team-all-conference-usa.aspx|archive-date=March 9, 2021|url-status=live}} On January 17, 2022, Young scored a career-high 30 points in a 96–67 loss against [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic]].{{cite news|title=Martin scores 20 to lead FAU over Charlotte 96-67|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401404466|website=ESPN.com|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 17, 2022|access-date=April 29, 2022}} He repeated on the First Team All-C-USA as a junior.{{cite press release|title=C-USA Postseason Awards Announced|url=https://conferenceusa.com/news/2022/3/7/mens-basketball-mbb-c-usa-postseason-awards-announced.aspx|website=ConferenceUSA.com|publisher=[[Conference USA]]|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2022}} As a junior, Young averaged 19.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game. On March 29, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility and later entered the transfer portal on April 7.{{cite web|first=Mathis|last=Gaglione|title=Charlotte's Jahmir Young declares for NBA Draft while maintaining collegiate eligibility|url=https://www.ninertimes.com/sports/charlottes-jahmir-young-declares-for-nba-draft-while-maintaining-collegiate-eligibility/article_5d98bf38-b113-11ec-b7d7-5b329d155c16.html|work=Niner Times|date=March 29, 2022|access-date=April 29, 2022}} On April 27, 2022, Young transferred to [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]]. Young, keeping his professional options open, also announced that he would continue with the NBA Draft process while maintaining his eligibility.{{cite web|title=Former Charlotte guard Jahmir Young commits to Maryland men's basketball|url=https://www.testudotimes.com/2022/4/27/23045156/former-charlotte-guard-jahmir-young-commits-to-maryland-mens-basketball|website=TestudoTimes.com|date=April 27, 2022|access-date=April 28, 2022}} In his first year with the program, Young, starring at point guard, led the renewal of the Maryland program under first-year head coach [[Kevin Willard]]. In 2023, Young was named second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] by both coaches and media.{{cite tweet|author=Big Ten Men's Basketball|title=A BIG shoutout to the #B1GMBBall Second Team All-Conference honorees! 🙌|number=1633155597960118272|user=B1GMBBall|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=June 30, 2024 }} ==Professional career== ===Grand Rapids Gold (2024–2025)=== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Young joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS ANNOUNCE 2024 NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER AND MINI-CAMP SCHEDULE|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-announce-2024-nba-summer-league-roster-and-mini-camp-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=August 1, 2024}} and on July 31, 2024, he signed with them.{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN JAHMIR YOUNG, GABE MCGLOTHAN, AND JAYLIN WILLIAMS TO EXHIBIT-10 CONTRACTS WITH THE GOLD|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-jahmir-young-gabe-mcglothan-and-jaylin-williams-to-exhibit-10-contracts-with-the-gold|website=NBA.com|date=July 31, 2024|access-date=August 1, 2024}} However, he was waived on October 8{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN WILL RICHARDSON, ANDREW FUNK, AND CHARLES BEDIAKO|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-will-richardson-andrew-funk-and-charles-bediako|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2024|access-date=October 8, 2024}} and on October 28, he joined the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].{{cite web|title=Gold Finalize 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/gold-finalize-2024-25-training-camp-roster/n-6160538|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} ===Chicago Bulls (2025)=== On February 19, 2025, Young signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |title=Bulls sign Jahmir Young to two-way contract |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-jahmir-young-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2025-02-22 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} He made his NBA debut on March 4 against the [[2024–25 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]], recording one rebound and one assist.{{Cite web|title=Former Maryland Star Jahmir Young On Making NBA Debut, Connecting With Fellow Terps|url=https://pressboxonline.com/2025/03/19/former-maryland-star-jahmir-young-on-making-nba-debut-connecting-with-fellow-terps/|access-date=April 3, 2025|website=pressboxonline.com|language=en}} Young made six total appearances for Chicago during his rookie campaign, averaging 1.8 points, 0.5 rebounds, and 1.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jahmir Young 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433133/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=June 19, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He was waived by the Bulls on July 20. ===Miami Heat (2025–2026)=== On August 20, 2025, the [[Miami Heat]] signed Young to an [[Exhibit 10]] contract. On October 18, the Heat converted Young's contract into a two-way contract.{{Cite web |date=2025-10-18 |title=Heat Convert Jahmir Young To Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-convert-jahmir-young-to-two-way-contract |access-date=October 24, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On April 10, 2026, Miami signed Young to a two-year, standard contract after a roster spot was cleared with the release of [[Terry Rozier]].{{Cite web|title=Heat waive Rozier, use roster spot to sign Jahmir Young|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48447174/sources-heat-waive-embattled-guard-terry-rozier|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He made 14 appearances for the Heat during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 1.8 points, 0.3 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jahmir Young 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433133/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=June 19, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
